messages:
Sam (sales): Quick sync — Acme wants 99.5% success SLA for their chat. Profile: ~100 TPS steady, 500 concurrent sessions, avg ~250 tokens/request, spikes to ~1.2k TPS for 2–3 min. They want reserved GPUs + autoscale plan. Qs: how many reserved GPUs for runway, prewarm strategy, spot fallback, and billing during AZ failover? Need wording for pricing appendix today.

Priya (eng-runtime): Quick ballpark calc below. Need to validate with exact model/quantization but useful for the appendix.
```
tokens_per_sec = TPS * avg_tokens = 100 * 250 = 25_000
gpu_throughput = 12_000  # tokens/sec per GPU (prod-quantized, A10x2-equivalent)
gpus_needed = ceil(tokens_per_sec / gpu_throughput) = 3
```
Rule of thumb: reserve 3 GPUs covers steady; reserve 4 if you want ~30% runway for SLO headroom + canaries. Autoscale: allow burst to a shared burst pool (on-demand) up to 2–3x; use prewarm credits for cold-start sensitive canaries.

Olivia (solutions): For the contract appendix I recommend: baseline reserved = 4 GPUs, monthly commitment; burst/overage billed per-token at on-demand rate; include 200 prewarm-credit minutes per month for warm replicas. I'll draft wording. :memo: 

Raj (eng-sre): Notes on AZ failover and billing: prefer warm replica pairs in a second AZ (keeps KV/kv-cache warm). During failover we will route traffic and spin up additional GPUs in failover AZ — that consumes active GPU hours and will be billed as on-demand/burst usage unless customer increases reserved footprint in both AZs. Need explicit contract language: "Reserved covers primary AZ baseline only; cross-AZ compute consumed in failover is billable as burst/on-demand." :warning:

Sam (sales): Customer asked specifically about spot instances for cost savings during burst windows — are we comfortable recommending them for latency-sensitive inference?

Priya (eng-runtime): Short answer: not for primary low-latency path. Spot is usable for noncritical background tasks (batch embedding/rerank) or as an extra ephemeral pool for non-SLA traffic. If they insist, we can provide an optional spot-burst design but must include: 1) higher pre-provision buffer (20–40%), 2) fast warm-fallback to on-demand, 3) clear SLAs exclusions for spot interruptions.

Olivia (solutions): I'll add a small table to the appendix: baseline reserved 4 GPUs -> predictable monthly fee; burst on-demand -> per-token/VM billed; spot-burst -> optional discounted rate with exclusions.

BillingBot: Reminder: draft pricing appendix templates are at https://redwood.internal/templates/pricing-appendix (link)

Raj (eng-sre): Operational runbook created (stub): https://go/runbooks/acme-runway — includes prewarm steps, canary traffic cutover, and post-failover reconciliation.

Sam (sales): Awesome — Olivia, Priya, Raj: please drop finalized appendix wording and the short justification (calc + risks) in this thread by EOD. I need to attach to the term sheet. Thanks! :pray:
